stem: Researchers studying endogenous hormones perform an animal experiment in which the levels of various substances are measured in the cerebrospinal fluid after application of noxious stimuli.  One of the compounds that increases is a peptide with a strong affinity for opioid delta and mu receptors.  Which of the following substances is produced from the same precursor as this peptide?​‌​‌​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​​​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​​​​​​‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌
explanation:
In this experiment, the concentration of a peptide with an affinity for opioid receptors increases following noxious stimulation.  This peptide is likely an endogenous opioid (eg, endorphin), which is secreted by neurons in response to nociceptor activation (eg, tissue injury) and functions to modulate pain perception.

Each of the endogenous opioid peptides is cleaved from a larger precursor protein.  One such precursor protein is proopiomelanocortin (POMC), which undergoes variable posttranslational modifications (eg, enzymatic cleavage) to yield smaller, mature peptides with diverse functions.  POMC-derived peptides include:

  • Beta-endorphin:  produces analgesic effect
  • Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH):  stimulates cortisol release
  • Melanocyte-stimulating hormone:  regulates melanin production

Therefore, the peptide likely identified in this experiment is beta-endorphin, which has a common molecular origin with ACTH.  The expression of these peptides varies depending on which cleavage enzymes are present in a certain tissue, but their functions are often complementary.  For example, in response to stress, neurons release beta-endorphin to reduce pain perception, and the anterior pituitary gland secretes ACTH to stimulate cortisol release and mediate the stress response.

(Choices B, C, and D)  Growth hormone and prolactin are structurally similar peptide hormones that are secreted by the anterior pituitary gland.  Somatomedin C, or insulin-like growth factor, is structurally similar to insulin and is released by the liver in response to growth hormone.  None of these hormones share a molecular origin with endogenous opioid peptides.

(Choices E and F)  Thyroid-stimulating hormone and vasopressin are peptide hormones but are not derivatives of the same precursor as endogenous opioid peptides.

Educational objective:Proopiomelanocortin (POMC) is a large precursor protein that undergoes posttranslational modifications (eg, enzymatic cleavage) to yield smaller peptides with diverse functions.  These peptides include beta-endorphin (endogenous opioid that reduces pain perception) and adrenocorticotropic hormone (modulates stress response via cortisol stimulation).​‌​‌​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​​​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​​​​​​‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌
